title: Sell Mineral Rights in Clarksburg, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Clarksburg, WV | Harrison County Seat
metaDescription: Clarksburg, WV is where WV's natural gas industry began, and its courthouse holds the deed record for it. We buy Harrison County mineral rights directly.
heroLead: Clarksburg is the Harrison County seat, and its courthouse deed books hold the paper trail for an industry that effectively started here, Hope Natural Gas Company was founded in Clarksburg in 1898.
intro: That history matters for anyone tracing mineral ownership today. Some of the oldest gas leases still on record in West Virginia originate from tracts in and around Clarksburg, and a fair number of them were never modernized. Layered on top is a century of subsequent leasing, right through the modern Marcellus and Utica development that's kept Harrison County active.

We buy oil and gas mineral and royalty interests in and around Clarksburg directly, working from the actual courthouse record for your tract rather than a general assumption about what an old Harrison County lease pays.

sections.heading: Where the paper trail runs deepest
paragraphs: Because Clarksburg is the county seat, its Clerk's office holds deed and lease books going back further, and in greater volume, than almost anywhere else in the state. That's useful for verifying old chains of title, but it also means Clarksburg-area tracts can carry more layered history: multiple leases, multiple reservations, multiple partial conveyances over more than a century.

sections.heading: Flat-rate leases from the earliest gas era
paragraphs: Some of the oldest surviving flat-rate leases in West Virginia trace to this part of Harrison County. If your family's lease predates the statutory conversion to a minimum one-eighth royalty and was never updated, you may still be receiving a decades-old flat payment. We check every Clarksburg-area lease for conversion eligibility before pricing it.

sections.heading: Modern Marcellus and Utica activity
paragraphs: Harrison County has remained an active leasing target for operators pursuing both Marcellus and deeper Utica/Point Pleasant zones. A Clarksburg-area tract may carry a legacy lease and a modern unit interest simultaneously, each paying under different terms.

sections.heading: Heirship across generations of county history
paragraphs: With this much history behind a tract, ownership has typically split across four, five, or more generations. We regularly untangle Clarksburg-area interests with a dozen or more heirs, several unreachable or deceased without a probated estate, and buy individual shares without requiring the whole family to agree.

faqs.question: How far back does the Clarksburg gas lease record go?
faqs.answer: Some Harrison County leases date to the late 1800s, around the founding of Hope Natural Gas Company. We can trace instruments that old when needed.

faqs.question: Is my family's old flat-rate lease still paying a fixed amount?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if it was never flagged for conversion. West Virginia sets a statutory minimum one-eighth royalty for flat-rate leases, but the conversion has to be applied. We check your specific lease.

faqs.question: Can a tract near Clarksburg have both an old lease and a new Marcellus unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common given the county's long leasing history. We review both instruments separately.

faqs.question: How many heirs typically hold a century-old Clarksburg mineral interest?
faqs.answer: It varies, but interests with this much history commonly involve eight to fifteen or more co-owners across multiple states.
